parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, an anti-discrimination law (2009) and hate-crime provision (2012) covering gender identity, partial state funding of surgery, and Pride now held annually under police protection are genuine positives. But the operative exposures are state-tolerated hostility with thin recourse: 20+ attacks on the LGBT centre since 2018 none properly sanctioned, a 2024 police raid involving alleged assault and torture with no sanction reported, politicians' hate speech, unsanctioned bias incidents, and public opinion where 57% call homosexuality a disease — a tier-2/tier-3 record. Enforcement of the protective laws is weak (one hate-crime conviction). The custodial search recommendation signals unresolved intake practice for detained trans visitors, but there is no documented universal exposure: no facility ban, border document friction, presentation offence or organised targeting. Weighing documented hostility plus failing remedy against real but under-enforced protections gives elevated risk.
